scoreRule: 1 point per correct MC item; 10 points maximum; local provisional grade only
description: Independent friendship-email reading assessment with original questions, pending pedagogical validation

questions.q: What was the biggest contrast between Lena's expectations and her first month abroad?
choices: The city looked less attractive than its photos.
Excitement about the exchange did not prevent loneliness.
Her host family refused to help her.
Her language course ended earlier than planned.
questions.explanation: Lena expected a holiday-like experience but felt unexpectedly isolated.

questions.q: Why were Lena's cheerful photos not a reliable picture of her life?
choices: They were all taken before she travelled.
They showed only the community radio station.
Her host family had edited the images.
They allowed her to hide the difficulties she was experiencing.
questions.explanation: She admits posting attractive pictures felt easier than confessing she was struggling.

questions.q: How did work at the community radio station change Lena's view of herself?
choices: She began to believe every new arrival was unhappy.
She decided to stop learning the local language.
Hearing migrants' stories made her own confusion feel less shameful.
She no longer needed to make friends outside the station.
questions.explanation: Other people's experiences helped her recognise that uncertainty is normal.

questions.q: Why does Lena value the radio work despite it being unpaid?
choices: The conversations matter more to her than the certificate.
She expects it to provide a high salary later.
She avoids working with other people.
She uses it mainly to collect photos for social media.
questions.explanation: She explicitly values people she meets more than the certificate.

questions.q: What does the bakery owner's experience suggest about adapting to a new place?
choices: Learning the language is the only challenge.
Baking familiar food solves social isolation.
Unspoken local rules can be more difficult than vocabulary.
Newcomers usually find new routines within a week.
questions.explanation: The owner says the hardest part was feeling that everyone else already knew the rules.

questions.q: What do the listener calls after the interview imply?
choices: The loneliness described by the baker is widely recognisable.
The station is preparing to close.
The bakery's recipes are too complicated.
All listeners have lived in the same neighbourhood.
questions.explanation: Several listeners recognise and respond to the experience of adjusting to a new place.

questions.q: Why does Lena hesitate to send a familiar school photograph?
choices: She has lost the original digital file.
It would avoid asking how Alex is actually doing.
Alex has said not to discuss their exams.
She worries that the photograph is embarrassing.
questions.explanation: She realises that a nostalgic photo would again replace a genuine conversation.

questions.q: How does Lena acknowledge a possible effect of her posts on Alex?
choices: She claims Alex must envy her travel photos.
She says Alex has misunderstood every message.
She thinks Alex no longer wants to be friends.
Her posts may have made Alex feel excluded from her life.
questions.explanation: Lena explicitly recognises Alex could have felt left out of her curated updates.

questions.q: What makes Lena's invitation considerate rather than demanding?
choices: She expects Alex to speak at the public event.
She insists that Alex buy a particular gift.
She offers a call as an alternative and no public performance is required.
She promises to pay every expense of Alex's visit.
questions.explanation: Lena provides options and removes social pressure from the invitation.

questions.q: What change in their communication is Lena really requesting?
choices: More honest conversations instead of only attractive online updates.
More frequent photographs of Rotterdam's buildings.
A shared certificate from the radio station.
A visit every week regardless of distance.
questions.explanation: The final paragraph asks for an actual conversation rather than another smiling photograph.
